faqs.question: What is Net Impact at Indiana University?
faqs.answer: Net Impact Indiana University is the undergraduate chapter of Net Impact, a global nonprofit network, at IU's Kelley School of Business. It's a student-led club focused on sustainable business, nonprofit consulting, community service and social impact careers.

faqs.question: Who can join Net Impact IU?
faqs.answer: Any Indiana University Bloomington undergraduate can join, from any major and any year. Membership applications are open all year. Fill out the membership form on the Join page to get started.

faqs.question: Does it cost money to join?
faqs.answer: Semester dues apply. Details are shared at the first general meeting of each semester.

faqs.question: When and where does Net Impact IU meet?
faqs.answer: General meetings are Mondays from 7:00 to 8:00 pm during the semester. Each week's room and topic are posted in the Net Impact IU GroupMe and on Instagram at @netimpact_iu.

faqs.question: What are Net Impact project teams?
faqs.answer: Project teams are semester-long consulting engagements for local nonprofits. Each team has one project lead and five consultants. Applications typically open the second week of each semester, followed by about two weeks of interviews, and applicants can rank the projects they want.

faqs.question: Is this the same as Kelley's MBA Net Impact chapter?
faqs.answer: No. Kelley also has a graduate Net Impact chapter for MBA students. Net Impact Indiana University is the undergraduate chapter.

faqs.question: How can my nonprofit work with Net Impact IU?
faqs.answer: Email envbus@iu.edu with a short description of your organization and the help you need. For fall projects, discovery calls run in July and August and student teams kick off in October.
